title: The Process of Becoming a “Spider-Man”
passage: You probably know of many animals in which the males and females look very different. Male lions, for example, have beautiful manes, while lioness do not. In birds, males tend to be beautifully colored, while the females are not—just think of ducks, chicken, or peacocks. But do you know how to distinguish spider-men and -women? Usually, female spiders are bigger, but only if they are well-fed. Females can also be a different color than the males of their species, but this is not true for all species. You can use another really safe trick to identify a male spider. In front of their four walking legs, both spider males and females have another pair of appendages, the pedipalps. The pedipalps are used for many of the spider skills explained above, like feeding, sensing, catching prey, and mating. And exactly on the tip of these pedipalps only adult male spiders have a specialized organ, which looks like boxing gloves.
sentencesPartEndsAfter: Females can also be a different color than the males of their species, but this is not true for all species.

The plural subject 'the females' needs 'are' ('the females are not beautifully colored').
'Know how to' + verb means to know the way to do something.
The sentence compares body size: a spider gets bigger only if it eats well.

'This is not true for all species' means the statement does not apply to every species.

title: Stay safe at the beach!
passage:
When going to the beach, find out which ones have lifeguards. Always try to visit beaches that have lifeguards watching the swimmers. The lifeguards on duty will put red and yellow flags on the beach to show you where it is safe to swim.

Many people find it hard to see a rip current in the sea. Rip currents are like fast-flowing rivers that can pull even strong swimmers away from the beach.

This is why it is better to swim between the lifeguard flags.

If you get pulled out by a rip current, try not to panic. Try to swim to the left or to the right of the current's flow. Don't try to fight the current or to swim against the current. That will make you tired and more scared.

To be safe when you visit the beach, you should always listen to the lifeguards. And make sure that you stay between the red and yellow flags on the beach. The flags show you where the currents are safe.

title: Detecting Ghostlike Neutrinos: Tiny Messengers From the Universe
passage:
Neutrinos are very light particles with no electric charge. They are emitted when unstable atomic nuclei decay. Such radioactive decay happens all around us. Minerals in rocks and even potassium in bananas decay to produce neutrinos. But far more neutrinos come from the nuclear reactions in the sun than from any other source.

No matter what their source, neutrinos are completely harmless because they do not stick together or interact with much of anything. They stream from the sun and outer space and pass right through ordinary matter—even our own bodies and Earth itself—without us ever knowing. In that way, they seem a bit like ghosts—there, and yet invisible. But because neutrinos carry information about what is happening inside the hearts of stars and galaxies, scientists want to know a lot more about them. Neutrinos may even help us understand what was going on when our universe first formed nearly 14 billion years ago!
sentencesPartEndsAfter: No matter what their source, neutrinos are completely harmless because they do not stick together or interact with much of anything.

blanks.why: An adjective is needed before 'particles', and 'very light' describes how little they weigh.
'When' tells us at what moment neutrinos are given off: when nuclei decay.
The plural subject 'nuclei' needs 'decay', and the next sentence repeats the idea with 'Such radioactive decay'.
'All around us' means everywhere near us.
After 'to' we need a base verb, and decay produces (makes) neutrinos.
'Far more ... than' compares the sun with all other sources.
'No matter what' is a fixed phrase meaning 'whatever'.
An adjective is needed after 'completely', and the reason given (they do not interact with anything) shows they cause no harm.

missingSentence: They stream from the sun and outer space and pass right through ordinary matter—even our own bodies and Earth itself—without us ever knowing.
missingDistractors: The process of radioactive decay involves the emission of particles such as electrons, or of radiation in the form of gamma rays.
Every atom has in its center a very small nucleus.
For any one radioactive nucleus, it is not possible to predict when the decay process will happen.
missingWhy: It says neutrinos pass through everything without us knowing, which the next sentence compares to ghosts with 'In that way'.

highlights.answer: the nuclear reactions in the sun

highlights.answer: neutrinos carry information about what is happening inside the hearts of stars and galaxies

distractors: Neutrinos have a strong electric charge, so scientists can see them easily.

title: Socrates
passage:
As Socrates did not write down any of his teachings, secondary sources provide the only information on his life and thought. The sometimes contradictory nature of these sources is known as the Socratic problem, or the Socratic question.

Plato and Xenophon's dialogues provide the main source of information on Socrates's life and thought. These writings are the Sokratikoi logoi, or Socratic dialogues, which consist of reports of conversations apparently involving Socrates.

As for discovering the real-life Socrates, the difficulty is that ancient sources are mostly philosophical or dramatic texts, apart from Xenophon. There are no straightforward histories, contemporary with Socrates, that dealt with his own time and place. A corollary of this is that sources that do mention Socrates do not necessarily claim to be historically accurate, and are often partisan. For instance, those who prosecuted and convicted Socrates have left no testament. Historians, therefore, face the challenge of reconciling the various evidence from the extant texts in order to attempt an accurate and consistent account of Socrates's life and work. The result of such an effort is not necessarily realistic, even if consistent.
sentencesPartEndsAfter: As for discovering the real-life Socrates, the difficulty is that ancient sources are mostly philosophical or dramatic texts, apart from Xenophon.

blanks.why: After 'did not' we need a base verb, and 'write down his teachings' means put them on paper.
'Secondary sources' are writings by other people; the plural matches the verb 'provide'.
'Sources' is plural, so it needs 'these', which points back to the sources just mentioned.
'Is known as' gives the name of something, here 'the Socratic problem'.
'A source of information' is a common phrase, and a noun is needed after 'of'.
'Which' starts a clause about things (the dialogues); 'who' is only for people.
'As for' is a fixed phrase meaning 'when it comes to'.
A singular noun is needed after 'the' and before 'is'; the sentence explains what makes finding the real Socrates hard.

missingSentence: Historians, therefore, face the challenge of reconciling the various evidence from the extant texts in order to attempt an accurate and consistent account of Socrates's life and work.
missingDistractors: Many thought Socrates was one of the sophists.
He wanted to base values on reason instead of on unchallenged traditional beliefs.
Primary sources, when we have them, are considered more valuable than other sources because they are as close in time as we can get to the events being studied.
missingWhy: 'Therefore' draws a conclusion from the problems with the sources, and 'such an effort' in the last sentence refers to this attempt to build an accurate account.

highlights.question: What is the conflicting nature of the sources about Socrates called?
highlights.answer: the Socratic problem, or the Socratic question

highlights.question: What kind of writing about Socrates's own time and place does not exist?
highlights.answer: straightforward histories, contemporary with Socrates

idea.answer: Because Socrates wrote nothing himself, we can learn about him only through other people's writings.
distractors: Socrates wrote many books about his life that historians still read today.
Primary sources are more useful than other sources because they come from the time being studied.
Historians agree that the ancient sources give an accurate picture of Socrates's life.
idea.why: The first sentence says Socrates did not write down his teachings, so secondary sources provide the only information on his life.

title: The boy and the jackal
passage: One day Jackal felt sick. He tried drinking water, but that made his stomach swollen. He tried eating grass but still his stomach hurt. Jackal decided that only the medicine of man would help him so he dragged himself off to the clinic in the town. "Auwwwh" said the nurse when she saw the bedraggled jackal, "this place is for sick people, not animals. Go away!" Now Jackal was a clever animal, so sick as he was, he made a plan. He asked a boy called Ernst who was sitting outside the clinic, to help him by fetching the medicine from the nurse. "If you do this for me, I will give you a fat, fresh bird for you cooking pot, everyday." Ernst was hungry and anyway, he felt sorry for the sick jackal, with his drooping whiskers and his tail hanging like a rag, so he went in and got the medicine and gave it to the jackal. Jackal licked up all the medicine at once and immediately his ears stood up and his tail lifted.

title: Protein Structure
passage:
As discussed earlier, the shape of a protein is critical to its function. To understand how the protein gets its final shape or conformation, we need to understand the four levels of protein structure: primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary.

The unique sequence and number of amino acids in a polypeptide chain is its primary structure. The unique sequence for every protein is ultimately determined by the gene that encodes the protein. Any change in the gene sequence may lead to a different amino acid being added to the polypeptide chain, causing a change in protein structure and function. William Warrick Cardozo showed that sickle-cell anemia is caused by a change in protein strucure as a result of gene encoding, meaning that it is an inherited disorder. In sickle cell anemia, the hemoglobin β chain has a single amino acid substitution, causing a change in both the structure and function of the protein. What is most remarkable to consider is that a hemoglobin molecule is made up of two alpha chains and two beta chains that each consist of about 150 amino acids. The molecule, therefore, has about 600 amino acids.
sentencesPartEndsAfter: Any change in the gene sequence may lead to a different amino acid being added to the polypeptide chain, causing a change in protein structure and function.

blanks.why: A singular noun is needed before 'of a protein is', and the next sentence talks about the protein's 'final shape'.
'A protein' is a singular thing, so the possessive is 'its'.
'Understand how' asks about the way the protein gets its shape.
After 'a' we need a singular noun, and amino acids are joined in a 'polypeptide chain'.
'Every' is followed by a singular noun ('every protein'); the other words need a plural.
'Is determined by' is a passive verb meaning 'is decided by'; the gene decides the sequence.
After 'may' we need a base verb, and 'lead to' means 'cause' (we cannot say 'cause to' or 'bring to' here).
'Being added to the chain' is passive: the amino acid is put into the chain.

missingSentence: In sickle cell anemia, the hemoglobin β chain has a single amino acid substitution, causing a change in both the structure and function of the protein.
missingDistractors: When protein is digested, it is broken down into amino acids.

title: Postindustrial Society
passage:
Information societies, sometimes known as postindustrial or digital societies, are a recent development. Unlike industrial societies that are rooted in the production of material goods, information societies are based on the production of information and services.

Digital technology is the steam engine of information societies, and computer moguls such as Steve Jobs and Bill Gates are its John D. Rockefellers and Cornelius Vanderbilts. Since the economy of information societies is driven by knowledge and not material goods, power lies with those in charge of storing and distributing information. Members of a postindustrial society are likely to be employed as sellers of services—software programmers or business consultants, for example—instead of producers of goods. Social classes are divided by access to education, since without technical skills, people in an information society lack the means for success.

'Material goods' are physical things that are made and sold.

title: The Era of Decline
passage: Beginning around 1800 BCE, the centuries of trade between the Indus valley and Mesopotamia came to an end. Over the next four centuries, the cities of the Indus River valley were slowly depopulated, and the civilization declined, likely in stages. Why and how this decline occurred remains unknown. One common view is that it was related to regional climate change. Around 2000 BCE, the floodplain of the Indus River shifted dramatically, creating dry river beds where cities had been and water once flowed. Changes in the pattern of seasonal wind and rainfall, known as the monsoon in South Asia, may have caused these environmental effects. Without a secure source of water for drinking and irrigation, the cities would have suffered declines in population. Another theory suggests that centuries of environmental degradation caused by urbanization and large population growth made the land unsuitable to human populations. Still other views point to the possibility of tectonic activity that changed the course of the rivers, or even epidemic disease that decimated the population.
sentencesPartEndsAfter: Around 2000 BCE, the floodplain of the Indus River shifted dramatically, creating dry river beds where cities had been and water once flowed.

title: DNA Repair
passage: DNA polymerase can make mistakes while adding nucleotides. It edits the DNA by proofreading every newly added base. Incorrect bases are removed and replaced by the correct base, and then polymerization continues. Most mistakes are corrected during replication, although when this does not happen, the mismatch repair mechanism is employed. Mismatch repair enzymes recognize the wrongly incorporated base and excise it from the DNA, replacing it with the correct base. In yet another type of repair, nucleotide excision repair, the DNA double strand is unwound and separated, the incorrect bases are removed along with a few bases on the 5' and 3' end, and these are replaced by copying the template with the help of DNA polymerase. Nucleotide excision repair is particularly important in correcting thymine dimers, which are primarily caused by ultraviolet light. In a thymine dimer, two thymine nucleotides adjacent to each other on one strand are covalently bonded to each other rather than their complementary bases. If the dimer is not removed and repaired it will lead to a mutation. Individuals with flaws in their nucleotide excision repair genes show extreme sensitivity to sunlight and develop skin cancers early in life.
sentencesPartEndsAfter: In yet another type of repair, nucleotide excision repair, the DNA double strand is unwound and separated, the incorrect bases are removed along with a few bases on the 5' and 3' end, and these are replaced by copying the template with the help of DNA polymerase.

blanks.why: We say 'make mistakes' (not 'do mistakes'), and after 'can' we need a base verb.
The singular subject 'It' needs 'edits', and editing means checking and correcting.
'And then' shows what happens next, after the wrong base is replaced.
'During' + noun ('during replication') means 'in the time of'.
The plural subject 'enzymes' needs 'recognize': the enzymes find the wrong base before removing it.
'Another type of' means 'another kind of', and 'another' needs a singular noun.
'Along with' is a fixed phrase meaning 'together with'.
'With the help of' is a fixed phrase meaning 'using' or 'helped by'.

missingSentence: In a thymine dimer, two thymine nucleotides adjacent to each other on one strand are covalently bonded to each other rather than their complementary bases.

highlights.answer: by proofreading every newly added base

title: Clouds and Global Warming
passage:
A new scientiﬁc study says that global warming might make temperatures rise more than people think. The scientist who led the research said that, if emissions of greenhouse gases are not reduced, the planet will be at least 4C warmer by 2100. This is twice the level the world’s governments consider to be dangerous. The research shows that fewer clouds form as the planet warms. This means that less sunlight reﬂects back into space and this makes temperatures even higher. The way clouds affect global warming has been the biggest mystery in the study of future climate change.

Professor Steven Sherwood, at the University of New South Wales in Australia, who led the research, said that their work was new in two ways. First, it found what controls the cloud changes and, second, it did not accept the lowest estimates of future global warming; it believed the higher, more damaging estimates.
sentencesPartEndsAfter: This means that less sunlight reﬂects back into space and this makes temperatures even higher.

'If' gives the condition: the planet gets warmer if emissions are not reduced.
'Are not reduced' is passive, so it needs the past participle; reducing emissions means making them smaller.
'At least' is a fixed phrase meaning 'not less than'.
An adjective is needed after 'consider to be', and a temperature rise can be dangerous.
'Fewer' needs a plural noun, and clouds form in the sky and reflect sunlight.
Temperatures become 'higher' (we do not say 'taller'); 'even' before it needs a comparative.

highlights.answer: at least 4C warmer

idea.answer: Because fewer clouds form as the Earth warms, global warming may be worse than many people expect.
distractors: More clouds form as the planet warms, and this helps to cool the Earth down.
The new study accepted the lowest estimates of future global warming.
The world's governments believe a rise of 4C would be completely safe.
idea.why: The passage says fewer clouds form as the planet warms, so less sunlight is reflected and temperatures may rise more than people think.
